Title: Information on: What happened on the Trail of Tears?...
The Trail of Tears, also known as the Indian Removal, was a series of forcible removals of Native American tribes from their ancestral lands in the Southeastern United States to Indian Territory (present-day Oklahoma) between 1830 and 1850. This displacement primarily affected the Cherokee, Creek, Choctaw, Chickasaw, and Seminole nations, resulting from treaties negotiated by the U.S. government under President Andrew Jackson. The forced march led to the deaths of thousands of Native Americans due to disease, starvation, and exposure during the long and difficult journey, earning it the name "Trail of Tears."
--- End Document 2 ---
